title: Power Apps: form fill assistance using Microsoft 365 files in model-driven apps
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the on-by-default field conflicts with the briefing's own statement that the new source's default is unclear. The app control path omits Features and the setting itself, and its undocumented-API claim overlooks documented setting APIs. The cost rating also assumes additional licensing that the sources do not establish.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend form fill assistance in Power Apps model-driven apps to use Microsoft 365 files as a source.
claims.quote: We’re expanding form fill assistance in Power Apps to use Microsoft 365 files as a source, helping users turn existing content into form entries with less manual effort.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in-development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Android, iOS and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "iOS", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-04T00:02:09.
The roadmap description lists the Monthly release channel.
claims.quote:
Release Channel
Monthly

claims.claim: The roadmap description lists version 2701.1.
claims.quote:
Version
2701.1

claims.claim: The roadmap feature-scope field lists multiple enablement categories rather than an unambiguous default.
claims.quote: Admins or makers | Users (enabled by admins or makers) | Users (enabled by default) | Users (always enabled)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 files extension is on by default.
claims.quote: defaultState: "on"; "so the effective default is unclear"; "Whether the feature will be on by default."
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Retain the open question: the roadmap lists conflicting scope categories, and the Learn pages describe existing form-fill defaults, not a confirmed default for this extension.

claims.claim: Current form fill assistance can generate suggestions from app usage.
claims.quote: Based on the user's usage of the app, what information is already available in the form, and their frequently used data.
claims.fix: Introduce the current-feature background with its qualification: Learn describes form fill assistance as generally available in Dynamics 365 apps and in production-ready preview in Power Apps. Do not present current preview limits as the final design of the Microsoft 365 files extension.

claims.claim: Smart paste is a current source of form-fill suggestions.
claims.quote: Based on the copied text the user provides through the Smart paste capability.

claims.claim: Current file suggestions support uploaded txt, docx, csv, pdf and image files.
claims.quote: Supported file types are .txt, .docx, .csv, .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, and .bmp.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The current Files capability does not support files classified with sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Files classified with sensitivity labels aren't supported.

claims.claim: Suggestions from the Microsoft 365 files extension may draw on files the user can access.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files source locations permissions sensitivity labels licensing price admin control; form fill assistance file permissions. Opened Learn form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; they describe user-provided files and a separate Copilot Chat experience.
claims.fix: Replace the permission implication with: 'The roadmap says Microsoft 365 files become a source; Microsoft has not yet documented the extension's file-access boundaries.' Do not transfer the separate Copilot Chat experience's access description to this roadmap feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Current suggestions include citations identifying their source.
claims.quote: This icon is a citation, and identifies the source of a specific suggestion, such as "Records you have updated recently" or "Clipboard".

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Current suggestions are not saved until the user accepts them.
claims.quote: Suggestions are entirely optional and aren't saved in the app until you accept them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI suggestions require users to review their accuracy and appropriateness.
claims.quote: The suggestions are optional and AI-generated. Users should ensure these suggestions are accurate and appropriate before accepting them.

claims.claim: Fields with column security are not currently supported.
claims.quote: Fields that have column security aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: The documented current form-fill licensing requirements are per user.
claims.quote: The form fill assistance requires specific user licenses based on the product.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn requires a Power Apps premium licence for users of form fill assistance in Power Apps model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven app: The user must have a Power Apps premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn requires a Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium licence for form fill assistance in Dynamics 365 model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 model-driven app: The user must have a Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium license as outlined in Dynamics 365 License Guide.

claims.claim: Users without the required licence do not see the feature.
claims.quote: If the user doesn't have the license, the feature is hidden. This license enforcement gradually rolls out following the feature's general availability.
claims.fix: Append that licence enforcement rolls out gradually following general availability, rather than implying universal enforcement already.

claims.claim: Usage may be throttled.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or throttling. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits.

claims.claim: An additional charge specific to the Microsoft 365 files source is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files licensing price; form fill assistance Microsoft 365 licensing files. Opened Learn form-filling-assistance, its FAQ and powerapps-flow-licensing-faq. None publishes an incremental charge for this source.

claims.claim: Current in-app form fill assistance is available on the web with the modern look enabled.
claims.quote: Form fill assistance is available for all apps on the web where the modern, refreshed look is turned on.

claims.claim: The Allow form fill assistance property must be enabled for a column to receive assistance.
claims.quote: The Allow form fill assistance column property enabled for the column where form fill assistance occurs.

claims.where: rationale: impact; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Current form fill assistance depends on enabled environment feature settings.
claims.quote: At least one of the AI form fill assistance environment feature settings enabled.

claims.claim: The primary environment control is under Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.
claims.quote: The primary admin control for form fill assistance is moving to the Power Platform admin center under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the primary Copilot Data entry control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps form fill assistance Copilot settings API PowerShell; Copilot Settings API data entry; power-platform copilot-hub API. Opened form-filling-assistance, copilot-hub and the setting client API reference; none documents the primary Copilot control's API.

claims.claim: The legacy environment feature page is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI form fill assistance.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. Expand Product, and then select Features. ... AI form fill assistance

claims.claim: Legacy environment controls are being removed in favour of the Copilot settings experience.
claims.quote: The primary admin control moves to Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry. ... The following settings are removed from the Environment > Settings > Features page.

claims.claim: An API for the legacy environment switch as such is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill organization Web API; form fill assistance PowerShell; AIFormFillAssistanceEnabled API. Opened settings-features and form-filling-assistance. No legacy switch API was stated; documented app-setting overrides are assessed separately.

claims.claim: Model-driven app designer > Settings (app properties) is the complete path to the smart paste and toolbar controls.
claims.quote: When you select Settings from the command bar, select Features to enable or disable model-driven app features for the app. ... Form fill assist toolbar.
claims.fix: For the toolbar, use 'App designer > Settings > Features > Form fill assist toolbar' and require Save and Publish. The pre-check's missing phrase 'Model-driven app designer' is not itself an error; the missing Features step and actual setting are. Narrow this row to the toolbar unless a separately documented smart-paste path is supplied.

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for the smart paste and form fill toolbar app settings.
claims.quote: saveSettingValue ... Adds or updates the setting app value for the current app or the setting environment value for the current environment.
claims.fix: Replace the null with documented setting automation. The cited form-fill article identifies FormPredictSmartPasteEnabled and FormFileUploadEnabled as app settings. The client API documents saveSettingValue(settingName, value, saveSettingOptions), with overrideScope 2 for an app. Its Web APIs section also links SaveSettingValue; that action's reference documents SettingName, Value and optional AppUniqueName and SolutionUniqueName. Cite these references rather than saying automation is undocumented.

claims.claim: A separate switch specific to Microsoft 365 files as a source is not documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files switch API; form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files source admin control. Opened form-filling-assistance, settings-features, app-properties and copilot-hub. No source-specific switch was documented.

claims.claim: There is no API for the Copilot settings page.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps form fill assistance Copilot settings API PowerShell; Copilot Settings API data entry; power-platform copilot-hub API. Opened copilot-hub and form-filling-assistance. Neither states that no API exists.
claims.fix: Replace the absolute statement with 'Microsoft has not documented an API for the Copilot Data entry control as of November 2026.' Keep this distinct from the documented app-setting APIs.

claims.where: Governance controls: notes; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Makers can disable Allow form fill assistance for individual sensitive columns.
claims.quote: Allow form fill assistance (preview) ... You can disable for columns that might contain sensitive information, such as email address.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-field-portal to sources and identify the column property as preview.

claims.claim: The Copilot area in Power Platform admin center provides usage analytics for the data entry agent.
claims.quote: Admins can view usage analytics for the data entry agent and data exploration agent on the Power Apps page

claims.claim: Supported Microsoft 365 file locations for the roadmap extension are not yet specified.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files; form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files source locations permissions. Opened form-filling-assistance and its FAQ. They describe user-provided files, not locations supported by the roadmap extension.

claims.where: Open questions: sensitivity labels; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap extension's treatment of sensitivity-labelled Microsoft 365 files is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: form fill assistance Microsoft 365 files source locations permissions sensitivity labels licensing price admin control. Opened form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; the current upload limitation is stated, but no extension-specific label behaviour is given.

claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks readers to review.
claims.quote: "Review environment form fill settings and column properties." The table contains environment, app and source-switch rows, but no Allow form fill assistance column-property row.
claims.fix: Add a column-scoped Allow form fill assistance (preview) row. The UI documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-field-portal is Power Apps > Tables > table > Columns > column > Allow form fill assistance (preview). Research its automation separately before setting that side to null.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cost rating is medium because the existing feature requires premium user licences.
claims.quote: cost: "medium"; "Medium. Learn states form fill assistance requires Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium user licences."; "Any additional charge for the Microsoft 365 files source is not yet published."
claims.fix: Set cost to low for the known review and training effort, and rewrite its rationale to say that extension-specific additional licensing or charges are not yet published. The schema defines medium as add-on licences or predictable consumption; existing product licence prerequisites alone do not establish either for this change.
